newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia sets 4-5 pct 1997 GDP target - agency.
newsitem.headline: Estonia sets 4-5 pct 1997 GDP target - agency.

text.p: Estonia's government plans to discuss an economic programme that foresees 1997 gross domestic product (GDP) growth of four to five percent and inflation of 10 to 15 percent, the Baltic News Service agency said on Monday.
The agency quoted a document to be discussed at the regular cabinet meeting on Tuesday, which sets out the political programme of the government along with its priorities.
A spokeswoman for Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi told Reuters that she did not know the details of the document.
The agency also quoted the document as saying the government aimed to cut corporate income tax to 15 percent by 1998.
The document also reaffirms the country's commitment to a balanced state budget and a currency board, the agency added.

The kroon currency is pegged at eight to one German mark under a currency board, which means that any rise in local currency in circulation has to be backed by a rise in foreign hard currency reserves.

The agency also quoted the document as saying that Estonia would not use foreign or domestic loans to cover the current expenses of the state budget and would introduce measures to control the taking of loans by local governments.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has highlighted a growing public sector deficit in Estonia as an area of concern and is anxious to stop local authorities fuelling the deficit with too much borrowing.
